sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The verb form usually shows who is doing the action, so Hungarian often leaves the subject pronoun unstated.

Olvasok already means ‘I read’ — tacking Én in front (Én olvasok) isn’t wrong, but it’s like saying ‘I, I read’; the ending has already told you who. Hungarian only bothers stating the pronoun for emphasis or contrast, not as a grammatical requirement the way English needs it.
